title: Do not let their rejection eat you up.
subtitle: Comfort for the one whose message is refused
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah told the Prophet ﷺ {idea}not to grieve over those who disbelieve{/idea}. Their return is to Allah, who will tell them what they did. {idea}Nothing in their hearts is hidden from Him.{/idea}
now: You keep sending your brother reminders and he leaves them on read. You lie awake replaying the last argument. {idea}Your part is to be sincere and kind.{/idea} Where his heart goes is between him and Allah.
old: If someone I love rejects the truth, it is my failure.
new: I carry the message with care. The hearts belong to Allah.
try: Make dua for one person you worry about, then let the worry rest with Allah tonight.

title: Enjoyment for a little while, then a heavy outcome.
subtitle: The short shelf life of comfort without faith
then: Ibn Kathir says this enjoyment is {reward}in this world{/reward}, and it is brief. After it comes a punishment that is hard to bear. He links it to 10:69-70, where {trap}worldly enjoyment is followed by the return to Allah{/trap}.
now: The weekend that flew by. The holiday that ended before you unpacked. {idea}A whole life feels like that at the end.{/idea} The question is not whether you enjoy it, but what you send ahead while you do.
old: I have plenty of time to sort out my priorities later.
new: This life is a little while, so what I do with it matters now.
try: Look at how you spent yesterday's free hour, and give one hour this week to something lasting.

title: They admit Allah created everything, then live as if not.
subtitle: Knowing the Creator is not the same as living by it

row.title: I believe, so I am fine

then: Ibn Kathir says the Makkan idol worshippers {idea}admitted that Allah alone created heaven and earth{/idea}. Yet they still worshipped things they knew He had created. {trap}Their own answer was the proof against them.{/trap}
now: Ask yourself who provides, and you answer Allah instantly. Then payday comes and the fear is about the boss, the market, the bonus. {trap}The answer is right, but the heart lives by another.{/trap}
old: I know Allah is the Creator, so my faith is sorted.
new: Knowing He created everything should change who I fear and hope in.
try: When you worry about money today, say Alhamdulillah and remind yourself who provides.

title: Everything belongs to Him, and He needs nothing.
subtitle: Al-Ghani, the Praiseworthy
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}He has no need of anyone or anything{/idea}, and everything else is in need of Him. He is praised for all that He creates and decrees, in every affair.
now: Your name is on the lease. Your phone, your car, your account. It feels like yours. {idea}Everything you hold is on loan{/idea} from the One who needs none of it, and gave it anyway.
old: What I worked for is simply mine.
new: All I have belongs to Allah, who needs nothing and still gives.
try: Give away one thing you own today that someone else needs more than you.

title: Every tree a pen, every sea ink, and still not enough.
subtitle: The Words of Allah have no end
then: Ibn Kathir says the number seven means {idea}a large amount, not a literal count{/idea}. The pens would break and the ink run dry. The Prophet ﷺ said in his prayer: {idea}I cannot praise You enough.{/idea}
now: You have a cloud full of notes, a library app, a search engine. It feels like everything can be known. {idea}Stand by the sea for a minute{/idea} and picture it as ink. Then picture it running dry.
old: I already understand most of what there is to know about Allah.
new: What I know of Allah is a drop. His Words never run out.
try: Learn the meaning of one Name of Allah you did not know well, today.

title: Raising all of humanity is as easy as raising one.
subtitle: Creation and resurrection are one command
then: Ibn Kathir says creating and resurrecting all of mankind is, to Allah's power, {idea}like creating one soul{/idea}. He hears all they say and sees all they do, {idea}as if hearing and seeing a single person{/idea}.
now: A crowded train at rush hour. Thousands of faces, and you feel like no one. {idea}To Allah you are not lost in the crowd.{/idea} He hears you as clearly as if you were the only one speaking.
old: With so many people, Allah cannot really notice me.
new: He hears and sees me as fully as if I were the only one.
try: In your next dua, speak to Allah about one small personal thing you thought too minor.

title: Night slides into day, and the sun keeps its course.
subtitle: The steady order of time
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah takes from the night and adds to the day, {idea}as in summer, then the reverse in winter{/idea}. The sun and moon each run to an appointed term. He ends with: Allah is aware of what you do.
now: The clocks change and your prayer times shift. Maghrib creeps later through spring. {idea}The same precision runs your day{/idea}, and the same Lord is aware of what you do with it.
old: Sunrise and sunset are just times on a weather app.
new: Each shift of light is a sign of an exact Lord who sees my day.
try: Watch the sunset tonight, or check the time of Maghrib and pray it on time.

title: Allah is the Truth. Everything else called on is false.
subtitle: Why the signs are shown

row.title: Allah
sub: the Truth, Most High, Most Great

then: Ibn Kathir says He shows His signs {idea}so you may know He is the Truth{/idea}. Nothing could move an atom's weight without His permission. {trap}If everyone came together, they could not create a fly.{/trap}
now: The horoscope app, the lucky number, the influencer you treat like a guide. {trap}None of them can move an atom.{/trap} The One who runs the sun and the moon is the One worth calling on.
old: A bit of superstition or reliance on people is harmless.
new: Only Allah is real power. Everything else depends on Him.
try: Delete or mute one thing you check for reassurance that is not Allah.

title: Ships float by His favour, a sign for the patient and grateful.
subtitle: Patience in hardship, thanks in ease
then: Ibn Kathir says that if Allah did not {idea}give the water the strength to carry ships{/idea}, they would not sail. The signs are for {reward}one who bears hardship with patience and gives thanks in ease{/reward}.
now: The ferry, the cargo ship that brought your shoes, the flight over the ocean. You take it as engineering. {idea}It is also a favour.{/idea} The patient and grateful are the ones who notice.
old: Things work because of science, not because of a favour.
new: The laws that make things work are His favour too.
try: Next time you travel, say a dua of thanks as you set off.

title: Sincere in the storm, half-hearted back on land.
subtitle: Calling on Allah only when waves rise
then: Ibn Kathir says when waves covered them like mountains or clouds, {idea}they called on Allah alone{/idea}. Safe on land, some held back. He explains Khattar as one who {trap}breaks his promise{/trap}, and Kafur as one who forgets blessings.
now: The hospital corridor at 3am. You promise Allah you will change everything. The scan comes back clear, and a month later the promise is gone. {idea}Remember the corridor.{/idea}
old: I turn to Allah when things get serious.
new: The dua I made in the storm is a promise to keep in the calm.
try: Recall one promise you made to Allah in a hard moment, and do one part of it today.

title: A Day when no father can help his son.
subtitle: Do not be fooled by this life or the Deceiver
then: Ibn Kathir says even if a father offered himself for his son, {trap}it would not be accepted{/trap}. Do not let contentment with this life make you forget the Hereafter, and do not let {trap}Shaytan's empty promises{/trap} deceive you about Allah.
now: You tell yourself your parents prayed enough for the family. Or that your kids will sort out your dua later. {idea}On that Day each person stands alone.{/idea} Today is still yours to prepare for it.
old: My family's goodness will somehow cover me.
new: No one can carry me on that Day, so I prepare my own way now.
try: Pick one good habit you have left to others in your family, and do it yourself today.

title: Five things only Allah knows, including your tomorrow.
subtitle: The keys of the Unseen
then: The Prophet ﷺ called these {idea}the five keys of the Unseen{/idea} that no one knows but Allah. Qatadah said: you do not know, son of Adam, {trap}when you will die{/trap}. You might die tomorrow.
now: Your calendar has next month's meetings and a holiday booked. The pension forecast runs thirty years ahead. {idea}None of it is promised.{/idea} Plan, and also live today as if it counts.
old: I know roughly how my life will go.
new: Tomorrow is with Allah. Today is the part I am given.
try: Do one thing today you have been putting off for later, such as a call, an apology, or a charity.
